general_background.title: Oleylamine changes how sulfur is delivered
general_background.summary: An amine can convert elemental sulfur into soluble polysulfide species before metal sulfide nanocrystals form. How sulfur is made available from that solution affects whether new nuclei form or existing particles keep growing.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: From Sulfur−Amine Solutions to Metal Sulfide Nanocrystals: Peering into the Oleylamine−Sulfur Black Box

general_background.title: Acetate can be exchanged before colloidal growth
general_background.summary: Cadmium acetate can exchange with a long-chain carboxylic acid to make a feed better suited to a nonpolar liquid. That precursor conversion can change when the mixture supplies cadmium to nuclei and existing crystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Recent Advances in the Liquid-Phase Syntheses of Inorganic Nanoparticles

general_background.title: A primary amine can change surface growth
general_background.summary: Oleylamine can coordinate soluble metal species and bind exposed surface sites during colloidal growth. It can therefore change how rapidly precursors react and how readily the resulting particles remain dispersed.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Nucleation and size focusing
general_background.summary: A rapid change in precursor availability can create a short nucleation period followed by growth on existing particles. Growth can narrow the size distribution while material is supplied, whereas later ripening can consume smaller particles and change that distribution again.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution
